fs-fa-order.back: Scene safe (guns unloaded), call for help, stop big bleeding, breathing, keep warm.

fs-fa-ccc.front: What are the 3 steps of the first minute?
fs-fa-ccc.back: Check (scene and danger), Call (911 or SOS, location first), Care (bleeding first).

fs-fa-call-first.front: On a 911 call, what do you say first?
fs-fa-call-first.back: Your location. If the call drops, help still knows where to go.

fs-fa-911-tower.front: No bars from your carrier. Can 911 still work?
fs-fa-911-tower.back: Often yes: a phone can reach 911 through any carrier tower in range (BC Search and Rescue Association, 75%).

fs-fa-signs.front: Name 4 signs of life threatening bleeding.
fs-fa-signs.back: Spurting, flowing that will not slow, pooling on the ground, soaking through clothes. Also a missing limb or a confused, pale person.
fs-fa-signs.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Signs of life threatening bleeding: blood spurting, flowing and not slowing, pooling on the ground, soaking through clothes, a missing part of an arm or leg, or the person turning confused, pale and weak. Any one means act now and call 911.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Is it life threatening?</text><circle cx="70" cy="70" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="70" y="116" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Spurting</text><text x="70" y="134" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">pulses out</text><circle cx="200" cy="70" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="200" y="116" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Flowing</text><text x="200" y="134" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">will not slow</text><circle cx="330" cy="70" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="330" y="116" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Pooling</text><text x="330" y="134" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">puddle on ground</text><circle cx="70" cy="170" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="70" y="216" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Soaking</text><text x="70" y="234" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">through clothes</text><circle cx="200" cy="170" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="200" y="216" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Missing part</text><text x="200" y="234" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">arm or leg</text><circle cx="330" cy="170" r="26.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="330" y="216" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Confused</text><text x="330" y="234" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">pale, weak</text><rect x="72" y="254" width="256" height="30" rx="6" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="200" y="275" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">Any one: act now, call 911</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-ladder.back: Press, pack, tourniquet. Climb only as far as you need.

fs-fa-pack-where.front: Which wounds get packed instead of a tourniquet?
fs-fa-pack-where.back: Deep wounds in the groin, armpit or side of the neck. Not the chest or belly.
fs-fa-pack-where.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Step 3: for a deep wound in the groin, armpit or neck where a tourniquet cannot go, stuff gauze into the wound until it is full.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">3. Pack a deep wound</text><ellipse cx="200" cy="170" rx="70" ry="34" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><ellipse cx="200" cy="170" rx="28" ry="12" fill="#c0392b"/><path d="M120 90 Q170 110 190 160" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="12" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M120 90 Q170 110 190 160" fill="none" stroke="#9a9a8f" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="110" y="80" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Gauze in, finger first</text><text x="200" y="238" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">Groin, armpit, neck</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Fill the wound to the top</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-pack-hold.front: After packing a wound, how long do you press on top?
fs-fa-pack-hold.back: At least 3 minutes, then wrap tight. Do not peek.

fs-fa-tq-when.front: When does a tourniquet go on?
fs-fa-tq-when.back: Life threatening bleeding from an arm or leg that direct pressure cannot control.

fs-fa-tq-where.back: Above the wound on the heart side, never on a joint. Distance: 5 to 8 cm or 5 to 10 cm depending on source (VERIFY with your instructor).
fs-fa-tq-where.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Two sources give different tourniquet distances above the wound: 5 to 8 centimetres (2 to 3 inches) in one, 5 to 10 centimetres (2 to 4 inches) in the Canadian Red Cross sheet. Both say above the wound on the heart side. Not settled: verify in your first aid course.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">How far above? Two sources differ</text><rect x="20" y="128" width="310" height="44" rx="22" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="344" cy="150" r="24.0" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><ellipse cx="300" cy="150" rx="16" ry="7" fill="#c0392b"/><rect x="206" y="112" width="82" height="10" rx="2" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="247" y="104" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">5 to 8 cm</text><rect x="186" y="186" width="102" height="10" rx="2" fill="#4a7fb0"/><text x="237" y="216" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">5 to 10 cm</text><text x="70" y="104" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Heart side</text><text x="318" y="84" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">Wound</text><line x1="312" y1="90" x2="304" y2="130" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="302,138 308,131 299,129" fill="#c0392b"/><rect x="50" y="250" width="300" height="30" rx="6" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="200" y="271" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">VERIFY in your first aid course</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-tq-finish.front: How do you finish a tourniquet?
fs-fa-tq-finish.back: Twist till it stops, lock, clock: lock the rod in its clip, write the time, leave it on for the medics.
fs-fa-tq-finish.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Tourniquet step 5: write TQ and the time on the band or on the forehead. Do not loosen it. Leave it for the medics.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">5. Write the time</text><rect x="30" y="138" width="300" height="44" rx="22" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="344" cy="160" r="24.0" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><ellipse cx="250" cy="160" rx="16" ry="7" fill="#c0392b"/><rect x="158" y="130" width="24" height="60" rx="4" fill="#e8590c" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="140" y1="124" x2="200" y2="124" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="7" stroke-linecap="round"/><rect x="220" y="60" width="150" height="62" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="98" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">TQ 13:42</text><text x="290" y="240" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">Do not loosen it</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">TQ plus the time. Leave it on</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-tq-second.front: First tourniquet as tight as it goes, still bleeding?
fs-fa-tq-second.back: Add a second tourniquet above the first, closer to the heart.

fs-fa-shock.front: Signs of shock and the care?
fs-fa-shock.back: Pale, cold, clammy, fast pulse, thirst, confusion. Stop bleeding, lay flat on a pad, cover, nothing to eat or drink.
fs-fa-shock.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Shock: signs are pale cold clammy skin, a fast pulse, thirst and confusion. Care: lay the person flat, keep them warm with a pad under and a cover over, and give nothing to eat or drink.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Shock: the body running out of blood</text><rect x="120" y="186" width="50" height="14" rx="5.0" fill="#e8590c"/><line x1="170" y1="194" x2="206" y2="195" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="8.0" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="110" cy="191" r="9.0" fill="#d9b48f"/><rect x="40" y="200" width="220" height="12" rx="4" fill="#8a9a6b"/><rect x="150" y="178" width="70" height="16" rx="3" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#9a9a8f" stroke-width="1"/><rect x="270" y="50" width="120" height="140" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="330" y="87" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Pale, cold</text><text x="330" y="106" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Clammy</text><text x="330" y="125" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Fast pulse</text><text x="330" y="144" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Thirsty</text><text x="330" y="163" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Confused</text><text x="140" y="248" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Lay flat, keep warm</text><text x="140" y="268" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Nothing to eat or drink</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-flush.front: How do you clean a dirty knife cut in the bush?
fs-fa-flush.back: Flush with at least 1 litre of drinkable water under pressure (squeezed bottle or pin hole bag), then cover.
fs-fa-flush.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Clean a cut, step 2: flush it with at least 1 litre of drinkable water from a squeezed bottle or a bag with a pin hole.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">2. Flush with 1 litre</text><rect x="30" y="168" width="300" height="44" rx="22" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="344" cy="190" r="24.0" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#b08a66" stroke-width="2"/><ellipse cx="250" cy="190" rx="16" ry="7" fill="#c0392b"/><rect x="150" y="60" width="50" height="80" rx="8" fill="#4a7fb0"/><rect x="165" y="50" width="20" height="12" rx="2" fill="#2f3a2b"/><path d="M178 140 Q210 160 245 182" fill="none" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="300" y="90" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">1 litre or more</text><text x="300" y="110" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">drinking water</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Squeeze hard. At least 1 litre</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-infect.back: Spreading redness, heat, swelling, pus, a red streak, fever. See a doctor.

fs-fa-knife.front: Two habits that prevent gutting cuts?
fs-fa-knife.back: Cut away from you with fingers behind the blade, and wipe the handle so a bloody grip does not slide.
fs-fa-knife.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Knife safety when field dressing: cut away from your body with fingers behind the blade. A sharp blade slips less. Wipe the handle often so a bloody grip does not slide onto the edge.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Field dressing: cut away from you</text><ellipse cx="200" cy="170" rx="120" ry="45" fill="#8b5a2b"/><line x1="150" y1="120" x2="230" y2="120" stroke="#9a9a8f" stroke-width="6" stroke-linecap="round"/><rect x="110" y="112" width="40" height="16" rx="4" fill="#2f3a2b"/><line x1="240" y1="120" x2="288" y2="120" stroke="#2e7d32" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="300,120 288,113 288,127" fill="#2e7d32"/><ellipse cx="118" cy="150" rx="18" ry="10" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="118" y="92" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Fingers behind</text><text x="300" y="100" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d32" text-anchor="middle">Away</text><rect x="20" y="228" width="170" height="50" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="105" y="249" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Sharp blade</text><text x="105" y="268" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">slips less</text><rect x="210" y="228" width="170" height="50" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="249" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Wipe the handle</text><text x="295" y="268" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">often</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-sprain.back: Sit, look for a bad bend, cool in a cloth 10 to 20 minutes, wrap firm, foot up, then the 4 step test.

fs-fa-4steps.front: Hurt leg: what decides walk out or wait?
fs-fa-4steps.back: Can take 4 steps: wrap, poles, partner carries gear. Cannot: stay, splint, shelter, call for help.
fs-fa-4steps.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Flowchart for a hurt leg: can the person take 4 steps? Yes: wrap it, use poles, go slow with a light pack, the partner carries the gear. No: stay, splint it, make shelter and warmth, call 911 or send SOS. If bone shows or the foot is cold, blue or numb, call for help now.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Hurt leg: walk out or wait?</text><rect x="110" y="44" width="180" height="40" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="200" y="69" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Can take 4 steps?</text><line x1="150" y1="84" x2="100" y2="112" stroke="#2e7d32" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="90,118 104,118 97,106" fill="#2e7d32"/><text x="100" y="100" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d32" text-anchor="end">yes</text><line x1="250" y1="84" x2="300" y2="112" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="310,118 303,106 296,118" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="300" y="100" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="start">no</text><rect x="10" y="120" width="170" height="72" rx="8" fill="#eef5e6" stroke="#2e7d32" stroke-width="2"/><text x="95" y="143" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Wrap, poles, go</text><text x="95" y="161" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">slow, light pack.</text><text x="95" y="179" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Partner carries gear</text><rect x="220" y="120" width="170" height="72" rx="8" fill="#fbe9e7" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="305" y="143" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Stay. Splint it.</text><text x="305" y="161" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Shelter, warmth.</text><text x="305" y="179" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Call 911 or SOS</text><rect x="20" y="214" width="360" height="44" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="200" y="232" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Bone showing or foot cold, blue, numb:</text><text x="200" y="250" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">call for help now</text>
</svg>

fs-fa-splint.back: Do not straighten. Pad. Joint above to joint below. Ties off the break. Check warmth and feeling before and after.

fs-fa-kit.back: Tourniquet, pressure bandage, packing gauze, gloves, shears, marker and tape. On your body, same pocket every hunt.
fs-fa-kit.diagram:
